title: Saying “in” with -ssa and -ssä
summary: Build a common Finnish place form after choosing the vowel-harmony version of the ending.
objectives: Attach the ending to a stable word.
Keep your attention on the ending rather than an unrelated stem rule.

sections.title: The meaning of the ending
paragraphs: Finnish often expresses an English preposition by adding an ending to a word. The ending -ssa or -ssä usually means “in”.
The two endings have the same meaning. Vowel harmony chooses their spelling: back-vowel words use -ssa and front- or neutral-only words use -ssä.

sections.title: Build the form one step at a time
paragraphs: Start with the basic dictionary form. Decide whether the word needs the a-ending or ä-ending. Then attach the ending without a space.
Every word in this focused lesson has a stable stem. No consonant or final-vowel change is hidden inside the answer.

steps: sauna contains the back vowels a and u.
Attach it directly: sauna + ssa = saunassa.
myymälä contains the front vowels y and ä.
Attach it directly: myymälä + ssä = myymälässä.

commonMistakes: Do not write the ending as a separate word.
Do not translate every English “in” mechanically; this lesson covers the regular physical-place meaning.
Do not invent a stem change: every word in this lesson keeps the supplied stem.

practiceExercises.prompt: Practise the inside ending: sauna (“sauna”) → ____ (“in the sauna”)
practiceExercises.explanation: sauna has back vowels, so add -ssa directly: saunassa.
toimisto contains the back vowel o, so “in the office” is toimistossa.
